newsitem.title: USA: Mellon profits higher but hurt by credit card provision.
newsitem.headline: Mellon profits higher but hurt by credit card provision.

text.p: Mellon Bank Corp. Friday reported higher fourth-quarter results as stronger fee revenues from all its services offset an increase in provisions for credit card losses.
Net income rose to $194 million, or $1.34 a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $174 million, or $1.16 a share, in the year-ago period.
Mellon's full-year profits rose to $733 million, or a record $5.15 a share, from $691 million, or $4.46 a share, in 1996.

Pittsburgh-based Mellon raised its credit loss provision to $80 million from $35 million in the fourth quarter to pay for potential credit card loan losses, and increased it for the year to $155 million from $105 million.
Mellon said its 1996 results reflected an increase in fee revenue, partially offset by higher operating expense, higher credit quality expense and lower net interest revenue.

Fee revenue increased 21 percent to $2 billion in 1996 from $1.7 billion in 1995, due to gains in virtually every category of its fee-based services as well as a $57 million gain on the sale of an American Automobile Association credit card portfolio recorded in the fourth quarter.
Net credit losses in the fourth quarter tumbled to $36 million from $138 million in the 1995 period.
Mellon's stock edged down 25 cents to $73.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
